card: Allows Bitcoin Core nodes to run txindex concurrently with block pruning (-prune) if the index has no legacy file-offset entries. When looking up a transaction contained in a pruned block, GetTransaction, REST, and RPC methods (getrawtransaction, gettxoutproof) surface candidate block hashes so callers can fetch the block with getblockfrompeer and retry. Additionally, getrawtransaction at verbosity 2 gracefully omits fee and prevout fields when undo data is absent for fetched blocks. This addresses four long-standing user issues dating back to 2017 (#10609, #12651, #16182, #35240).
changed_since_previous: Added handling for missing undo data in getrawtransaction verbosity 2 so transactions can still be returned without fee/prevout when a block is fetched without undo data via getblockfrompeer, and added optional data payload support to JSONRPCError.
evidence: Resolves multiple long-standing feature requests to support txindex on pruned nodes: #10609, #12651, #16182, and #35240
Enabled by #35531 (merged), which replaced direct block file offsets with block hashes in txindex entries
problem: Pruned nodes have historically been prevented from enabling -txindex because legacy index records pointed directly to block file offsets on disk. Users with pruned nodes could not use txindex for raw transaction lookups, proof generation, or PSBT input resolution without maintaining a full unpruned chain.

risk.why: A bug in index lookups or RPC error handling could cause transaction retrieval failures or malformed responses across RPC and REST endpoints.

scope_notes: Touches the index subsystem, RPC/REST transaction lookups, and JSON-RPC error structures to pass optional error.data fields.
summary: Allows running -txindex concurrently with block pruning (-prune) when the index has no legacy file-offset entries. When a lookup via txindex or GetTransaction targets a pruned block, candidate block hashes are returned to the caller. RPC commands (getrawtransaction, gettxoutproof) and the REST /tx endpoint return these hashes in structured error responses so callers can fetch the missing block via getblockfrompeer, and getrawtransaction at verbosity 2 gracefully handles blocks lacking undo data.
